players.name: George Pickens
players.why: target of two expired offers (Watson + Nailor): e7d4703d died 9/9 10:18 PM, bf660050 died 9/12 12:35 PM, both unanswered. Week 1: 3 of 6 targets, 28 yards, 5.8, so his price is at its low while Watson's 32.7 is at its high, which is the best the 2-for-1 will ever look to a recency-biased manager. Rest of season he projects 234.1 vs Watson 156.3, and Nailor's 119.2 is unrealizable bench value
players.trigger: the Ayahuasca trigger FIRED 2026-09-16 (their first move of the season) and Alex was pinged; a third send is still his tap alone and has now been raised three times (9/12, 9/15, 9/16). Do not send it unasked. If he answers Re-send, file it the same day: the edge is Watson's 32.7 sitting next to Pickens' 5.8 and it decays with every week played

players.name: Bucky Irving
players.why: was a BUY flag (volume, unlucky on TDs); Irving-for-Stevenson was dead even on ESPN's screen. Week 1 closed that window: 20.3 points and national 'RB1 upside' coverage, so the market has repriced him upward, not down
players.trigger: the 9/7 trigger is void: it required his owner to be 0-2 and KC Breathmints are 1-0. Re-open only on the actual buy-low shape, two quiet weeks on maintained touches. Buying him now is paying the premium this entry existed to avoid

players.name: Chris Brooks
players.why: still a free agent 2026-09-16 at 14.3% rostered. Week 1 usage now known and it argues AGAINST him: 7 carries for 29 yards, 1 target, no catch, 2.9 points. He led SNAPS 38 to 30 but MarShawn Lloyd led CARRIES 13 to 7, and Lloyd is rostered by Goedel, Escher, Butkus. Rotowire reads Green Bay as riding the hot hand game to game while Jacobs is on the exempt list, which is the opposite of the predictable volume we rank on. Buying Brooks is buying the lesser half of a committee whose better half is already gone
players.trigger: Alex asked 2026-09-16 to be flagged on the week-2 Green Bay split specifically. Two ways it fires. MECHANICAL: own_jump 8 means roster-watch banners any 8-point rostered-percentage move, which is the market pricing a backfield winner faster than a box score reads. JUDGMENT, at the Tuesday routine: add him only on 50%+ of the Green Bay backfield (carries, not snaps, since snaps already misled once here); under 40% in a three-way split is noise and the entry stands pat. Roster is full at 16, so any add spends a drop and must clear Noel or Nailor on season projection, not on one week

players.name: MarShawn Lloyd
players.why: the other Packers back, on Goedel, Escher, Butkus
players.trigger: whichever of Lloyd and Brooks gets the touches is the buy; the other is noise

players.name: Josh Jacobs
players.why: commissioner's exempt list; pleaded no contest 9/10 to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage, and per Schefter the NFL may count time on the list as time served. Still on The Oprah Winfreys, 0.0 in week 1 and projected 0.0 for week 2
players.trigger: reinstatement with the role intact = buy-low from a frustrated owner; ask Alex. His owner is already visibly desperate at RB (see the Oprah Winfreys team entry), so a reinstatement is as likely to make them hold as to make them sell

players.name: Devaughn Vele
players.why: ours, rostered 9/9 off waivers, absorbing the New Orleans target share our IR'd Tyson vacated. Week 1 confirmed the role: 7 of 9 targets, 69 yards and a TD, 19.9
players.trigger: NOT a drop candidate any more; the 9/7 line calling him the first drop was written before a snap of his had been seen. Nine targets is a role. Promote to WR2 or FLEX on a second week at or above 20% target share, and re-read if the share falls under 15% for two straight weeks

players.name: Jauan Jennings
players.why: WAS on the list as the highest-volume receiver on the wire (6.0 targets on 82% snaps), but that was his 2025 role in San Francisco. In Minnesota in week 1 he drew ONE target and caught none, 0.0 points, in a 39-22 win. The volume thesis that put him here is refuted by the only week of evidence that bears on it
players.trigger: do NOT claim on his 114.8 season projection, which is priced on the old role. Needs 6+ targets in a single week to become interesting again; if week 2 is another 1-2 target game, delete this entry

players.name: RJ Harvey
players.why: ours; SELL flag (12 TDs on 42% snaps last year). Week 1 made the flag worse, not better: THREE carries, 8.1 points earned mostly on four catches and four kick returns. His 149.6 season projection is the softest number on our bench
players.trigger: sell high on any two-touchdown game, the following Tuesday. Separately, if he is still under 8 carries a game at week 4, stop treating him as protected RB depth and let him be the drop ahead of players projected below him

players.name: Jordyn Tyson
players.trigger: when his practice window opens, decide activation on the role, not the injury

teams.name: Ayahuasca Rodgers
teams.why: ACTIVE as of 2026-09-16, which kills the premise this entry was built on. Their first transaction of the season processed at 2:16 AM: a waiver claim swapping the Lions D/ST out for the Bengals D/ST, which is a deliberate matchup move, not an ESPN autopick. The standing counterargument to a third Pickens send, that the manager has never been in the room, is now false. Still 0-1 and holding Pickens

teams.name: The Oprah Winfreys
teams.why: the live trade lane. They offered Jonah Coleman for Kenneth Walker III at 10:04 PM on 9/14, minutes after Walker's 34.1 closed the Monday nighter, and they are starving at RB: Jacobs 0.0 on the exempt list, Cook 9.9, and a 97.6 week 1 that was the second-lowest winning score in the league. Our RB room is the deepest part of our roster and Trades wants us selling into exactly this need. They will open well below market, so counter rather than dismiss
